traveler: Haile Selassie I (Lij Tafari Makonnen, Ras Tafari)
title: The Hills Above Harar to the Rostrum at Geneva: the Lion of Judah, the Five Years of Exile, and the God He Never Claimed to Be
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Ejersa Goro, the birth in the hills
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia and the standard biographies agree on 23 July 1892. Coordinates corrected to 9 degrees 29 minutes north, 42 degrees 14 minutes east per Wikipedia's Ejersa Goro article; an earlier working figure of 9.25 placed the point some 26 km too far south.
stops.campa: In the hamlet of Ejersa Goro, in the hills east of Harar, a son is born to Ras Makonnen Wolde Mikael, governor of Harar and cousin to Emperor Menelik II. They name him Lij Tafari Makonnen. The house he is born into traces itself through the Solomonic line to Menelik I, son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, and holds the throne of Ethiopia by that descent. No survey fixes the hamlet on a modern map; the emperor will later build a church here, Kidane Mihret, so that the birthplace has a wall and a roof to be pointed at.
suggested_refs: The church of Kidane Mihret at Ejersa Goro, built by Haile Selassie to mark his birthplace
sources: Harold G. Marcus, Haile Selassie I: The Formative Years

stops.name: Harar, the viceroy's compound inside Jugol
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the childhood at Harar is attested in substance but no source reachable this session dates the years of tutelage, so the month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: The boy grows up inside Jugol, the walled old town, in his father's compound among mosques and merchant houses. Abba Samuel, an Ethiopian Orthodox monk, teaches him Ge'ez and scripture; Dr Vitalien, a Guadeloupean physician at the Harar court, teaches him French and the shape of a wider world. He learns Amharic law and European grammar in the same rooms. Harar is a caravan city with its own emirs in living memory, taken by Menelik seven years before Tafari's birth, and it is where he first watches a province being governed.
suggested_refs: The walled city of Jugol, Harar, and the compound of Ras Makonnen
sources: Harold G. Marcus, Haile Selassie I: The Formative Years

stops.name: Addis Ababa, the boy dejazmatch at Menelik's Gebbi
stops.date_confidence: attested for the appointment as Dejazmatch of Gara Mulatta at thirteen, dated 1 November 1905 in the chronology; the subsequent Selale and Sidamo governorships are attested to 1906 and 1907 without day dates.
stops.campa: At thirteen he is made Dejazmatch of Gara Mulatta and brought into Menelik's Gebbi, the hilltop compound of council halls and churches that anchors the new capital. Here he watches the machinery of the Solomonic state and the rivalries among the emperor's governors. His father dies the following year and the governorship of Selale passes to him; in 1907 he is given Sidamo, a province in the far south he has never seen. He is a boy holding provinces, and the soldiers who ride under his banner are twice his age.
suggested_refs: The Gebbi of Menelik II, Addis Ababa, seat of the Solomonic state
sources: Harold G. Marcus, Haile Selassie I: The Formative Years

stops.name: Harar, his father's province and a wife from Ambassel
stops.date_confidence: disputed and left disputed: Wikipedia states verbatim that 'Tafari was made governor of Harar in 1910 or 1911.' The year is pinned here to 1910 only to keep travel order, and the alternative 1911 is equally supported. The marriage to Menen Asfaw on 3 August 1911 is firmly dated, but no reachable source names the place of the wedding; Harar is where the couple then lived.
stops.campa: Menelik gives him his father's own province. He returns to Harar as its governor, to the walls and the compound where he was tutored, and rules from the seat Ras Makonnen held. In August 1911 he marries Menen Asfaw of Ambassel, a match that ties the house of Harar to the great families of the north. She is crowned with him nineteen years later and follows him into exile and back. Sixty-five years on she is buried beside him. The next summons north takes him out of the province for good and makes him regent of an empire.
suggested_refs: The governor's residence at Harar, held by Ras Makonnen and then by his son
sources: Harold G. Marcus, Haile Selassie I: The Formative Years

stops.name: Addis Ababa, proclaimed Regent
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The formal investiture as Ras Tafari Makonnen follows on 11 February 1917 and is carried in the pool as reconstruction rather than firm attestation.
stops.campa: Lij Iyasu, Menelik's grandson and designated heir, has alarmed the nobility and the church with rumors of conversion to Islam. The council deposes him and settles the throne twice over: Zewditu, Menelik's daughter, is made Empress, and Tafari Makonnen is proclaimed Crown Prince and Regent Plenipotentiary. He takes the title Ras Tafari. Sovereignty is split in two, hers the crown and his the government, and the arrangement holds for fourteen years. The name he takes here will one day name a religion he never asks for.
suggested_refs: The 1916 regency settlement dividing crown from government between Zewditu and Ras Tafari

stops.name: Segale, the army of Wollo broken
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day per Wikipedia's Battle of Segale. Coordinates approximate: the source locates Segale only as '40 miles north of Addis Ababa', which is the bearing and distance used here; an earlier working figure of 9.3667, 39.05 sat north-east of the capital and was wrong on both counts.
stops.campa: Negus Mikael of Wollo marches south to put his son back on the throne. The armies of the regency council meet him at Segale, north of the capital, and the troops of Fitawrari Habte Giyorgis break them. Ras Tafari has been regent for a month already when the battle is fought; the battle makes the appointment real. From here he governs an empire whose empress reigns over him and whose nobility outranks him in everything except position, and he spends the next twelve years quietly converting the position into the power.
suggested_refs: The Segale battlefield north of Addis Ababa, October 1916
sources: Harold G. Marcus, Haile Selassie I

stops.name: Geneva, Ethiopia seated among the nations
stops.date_confidence: the year 1923 is attested; the day date is the conventional one for the admission session and was not re-verified against League records this session. The Assembly met at the Salle de la Reformation before the Palais des Nations opened in 1937, but the hall used for this particular vote is not confirmed.
stops.campa: Ethiopia is admitted to the League of Nations. The delegation argues that membership will help suppress the slave trade still practiced inside the empire. It does not argue aloud that a seat at Geneva is a wall against Italian and British ambition. Ras Tafari has driven the application from Addis Ababa and is not in the hall for the vote. The Assembly seats an African monarchy among the recognized states of the world. Thirteen years later he stands in this city himself and asks the same body to mean what it voted.
suggested_refs: The Salle de la Reformation, Geneva, meeting place of the League Assembly before 1937

stops.name: Jerusalem, Deir Sultan on the roof of the Sepulchre
stops.date_confidence: the 1924 tour is attested as a list of cities, not as a dated itinerary; no source reachable this session gives arrival dates, so month and day default to 01 throughout the segment and the order follows Wikipedia's own listing.
stops.campa: On his first journey outside Ethiopia the regent comes to Jerusalem, where Ethiopian monks have held Deir Sultan on the roof of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre for centuries, in standing dispute with the Coptic and Greek churches over every doorway and cistern. He prays at the holy sites. The Kebra Nagast sends Menelik I from Aksum to this city, to the Temple Mount, to receive his father Solomon's blessing and to carry the Ark home. The regent arrives by steamship on a diplomatic tour, at the far end of the same claim.
suggested_refs: Deir Sultan, the Ethiopian monastery on the roof of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre

stops.name: Alexandria, the see that sends the Abuna
stops.date_confidence: attested as a stop on the 1924 itinerary; date undated as above. An earlier working version of this stop placed him at Cairo, which no reachable source supports: Wikipedia's itinerary names Alexandria.
stops.campa: The tour touches Alexandria, seat of the Coptic patriarchate from which Ethiopia has received its Abuna, its metropolitan bishop, since the fourth century. Until 1959 the head of the Ethiopian church is an Egyptian monk sent south by Alexandria, a dependency the regent intends to end. He walks through the city that has supplied the office since Frumentius. He also studies a modernizing state under British administration, which is the other thing he came a long way to look at.
suggested_refs: The Coptic patriarchate of Alexandria, source of the Ethiopian Abuna until 1959

stops.name: Paris, the regent photographed in a frock coat
stops.date_confidence: attested as a stop; undated as above.
stops.campa: Paris receives the regent among the victorious powers whose recognition he is courting. France holds Somaliland on Ethiopia's flank and the railway that runs from Djibouti up to Addis Ababa, which makes the audience practical as well as ceremonial. Newspapers photograph him in Western dress beside French officials, and the photographs travel: an African sovereign in a frock coat, filed by editors who had kept no column for such a thing. Twelve years on, the rail line he negotiates over here carries him out of his own country.
suggested_refs: The Franco-Ethiopian railway, Djibouti to Addis Ababa, subject of the Paris audiences

stops.name: London, Buckingham Palace and George V
stops.date_confidence: attested as a stop; undated as above. The content of the audience is not recorded in reachable sources and is left as a gap.
stops.campa: George V receives him at Buckingham Palace. Britain holds colonies on three sides of Ethiopia and carries weight at Geneva, and the Nile that waters Egypt rises in the Ethiopian highlands. The audience that matters most on the tour is also the one that commits to least. Nothing is settled about borders or rivers. The photographs do the work instead, circulating as evidence that Ethiopia has a modern head of state rather than the chieftain the European papers have been printing since Adwa.
suggested_refs: Buckingham Palace, audience of Ras Tafari with George V, 1924

stops.name: Gibraltar, the rock on the outbound leg
stops.date_confidence: attested as a stop on the itinerary; undated as above.
stops.campa: The ship calls at Gibraltar, the British fortress at the western gate of the Mediterranean, a coaling stop and nothing more on a long itinerary of ports and palaces. In 1936 he passes this rock again, sailing the other way, out of a country under Italian occupation, and transfers here from a naval vessel to an ordinary liner for the last leg to England. In 1924 nobody on the quay has any reason to note the passage. The symmetry is available only afterward, to people reading both dates at once.
suggested_refs: The Rock Hotel, Gibraltar, waystation of both the 1924 tour and the 1936 flight

stops.name: Athens, the tour closes among the ancients
stops.date_confidence: attested as the closing stop of the European leg; undated as above.
stops.campa: The European leg closes in Athens, where the Greek court receives him. Two states that call themselves ancient sit at one table negotiating a modern standing among the great powers, and the toasts do not leave the resonance alone. From here the party turns back toward the Mediterranean and the passage home. The regent has been received at Jerusalem, Alexandria, Paris, Luxembourg, Brussels, Amsterdam, Stockholm, London, Geneva, Gibraltar and Athens, and he carries the whole list back to Addis Ababa as evidence.
suggested_refs: The Old Royal Palace, Athens, final court of the 1924 tour

stops.name: Addis Ababa, crowned Negus by the Empress
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Zewditu crowns him Negus, king, a rank below her own and above every other man in the empire. It is a concession extracted rather than a gift: the regent has spent twelve years absorbing the powers of government while the Empress held the crown, and the nobility that resents him has run out of ways to stop him. Ethiopia now has an empress and a king at once, an arrangement nobody expects to hold. It holds eighteen months, and ends with a battle and a funeral in the same week.
suggested_refs: The 1928 coronation of Tafari Makonnen as Negus under Empress Zewditu

stops.name: Anchem, the last battle of the old kind
stops.date_confidence: date attested to the day; battlefield coordinates approximate, the site is not precisely fixed in any source reachable this session.
stops.campa: Ras Gugsa Welle, governor of Begemder and the Empress's estranged husband, marches against the king with a provincial army. At Anchem the royal forces break him and Gugsa is killed. It is the last battle of the old kind, nobles and levies contesting who shall hold the throne. Two days later Zewditu dies at the palace in Addis Ababa, of paratyphoid fever and complications of diabetes. The empire passes to Tafari Makonnen inside forty-eight hours. Fourteen years of manoeuvre finish inside a single week, and no army in Ethiopia is left that can contest it.
suggested_refs: The battlefield of Anchem, 31 March 1930, and the death of Empress Zewditu two days later

stops.name: Addis Ababa, St George's Cathedral: King of Kings
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He is crowned Negusa Nagast, King of Kings, at the Cathedral of St George, and takes the regnal name Haile Selassie, Power of the Trinity. Foreign delegations attend. Solomonic ritual runs beside motorcades, and the dispatches go out by telegraph to the wire services in Europe and America. The titles read out over him include Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah and Elect of God. Photographs of the crowning reach Jamaica within days, where they are read as something other than a coronation.
stops.quote: Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah, Haile Selassie I, Elect of God, King of Kings of Ethiopia. May it arrive for the honorable President of the Republic of Bolivia. Peace be with you.
stops.quote_source: Salutation of the letter announcing his ascension, addressed to the President of Bolivia, 1922 E.C. (1930); volunteer Wikisource translation from the Amharic, not a scholarly edition
suggested_refs: The Cathedral of St George, Addis Ababa, and the coronation regalia of 2 November 1930

stops.name: Aksum, the throne the Kebra Nagast gives him
stops.date_confidence: no journey to Aksum at this date is recorded anywhere; the pin marks the dynastic claim asserted at the coronation, and the date is the coronation's. The 225th-monarch count is traditional, not documentary.
stops.campa: The Kebra Nagast places the throne of the Solomonic line at Aksum. Makeda, the Queen of Sheba, travels north to Solomon in Jerusalem and returns bearing Menelik I, who goes up to the Temple Mount in his turn and carries the Ark of the Covenant home. The stelae field stands here, and the Chapel of the Tablet at St Mary of Zion holds what Ethiopia says is the Ark. The man crowned at Addis Ababa is counted, by that reckoning, the two hundred and twenty-fifth monarch of the line. He does not travel here to be crowned; the claim travels to him.
suggested_refs: The Chapel of the Tablet at St Mary of Zion, Aksum, and the stelae field
sources: sheba.journey.json, 'The Ark Enthroned at Aksum: the Lion of Judah'

stops.name: Addis Ababa, the constitution and the end of Jimma
stops.date_confidence: the constitution is attested to 16 July 1931. The Jimma absorption is dated 12 May 1932: Wikipedia's Kingdom of Jimma article records some 400 soldiers and a team of administrators arriving that day. Note that it was a kingdom whose rulers were titled Moti, not a sultanate, as an earlier working note had it.
stops.campa: He promulgates Ethiopia's first written constitution, a bicameral legislature whose members he appoints and whose powers descend from the crown, and which sets down in writing that the succession belongs to his own line and to no other. The following spring some four hundred soldiers and a team of administrators ride into Jimma and end the kingdom there, the last of the old southern monarchies, whose ruler Abba Jifar II has lately died. Centralization proceeds by document in the capital and by column in the provinces.
suggested_refs: The Ethiopian constitution of 16 July 1931
Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Jimma'

stops.name: Kingston, the coronation read as prophecy
stops.date_confidence: deliberately hedged. Wikipedia's Rastafari article dates the movement's development to 'during the 1930s' and names Leonard Howell among the preachers who proclaimed Selassie's divinity after the coronation, but gives no 1930 proclamation and no month. Howell's preaching is conventionally placed c. 1932-33, which is where this stop sits; the 1930 coronation is the trigger, not the date of the proclamation.
stops.campa: In Jamaica the photographs of the coronation reach readers of the Garveyite press, who have been told to look to Africa for the crowning of a Black king. Leonard Howell and other preachers proclaim that the man crowned in Addis Ababa is God returned, and take the regent's title, Ras Tafari, as the name of the thing they are founding. Marcus Garvey, whose movement supplies the prophecy, will reject the reading. Prince Hall had put the same verse of Psalm 68 into a Masonic charge at Charlestown in 1792: Aethiopia shall stretch forth her hands unto me.
suggested_refs: Leonard Howell's early preaching in Jamaica, c. 1932-33
Psalm 68:31 in the Garveyite and Rastafari readings
sources: prince_hall.journey.json, 'Charlestown, Aethiopia stretching forth her hands'
robert_finley.journey.json, 'A century after Finley, Garvey preaches return'

stops.name: Welwel, the wells in the Ogaden
stops.date_confidence: date attested to the day; coordinates for Welwel approximate, the wells are a desert site not consistently mapped.
stops.campa: Ethiopian and Italian forces clash at the wells of Welwel in the Ogaden, inside territory Ethiopia holds to be its own, over a garrison Italy has placed there. The incident gives Rome the grievance it has been waiting to be given. Haile Selassie takes the case to the League of Nations, which is what a member state is supposed to do, and the League appoints an arbitration commission, which is what the League does in place of acting. The commission is still sitting when the invasion is ready.
suggested_refs: The Welwel wells in the Ogaden and the League arbitration commission of 1935

stops.name: Rome, Palazzo Venezia: war declared on Ethiopia
stops.date_confidence: the interlocking mussolini journey file gives the year only, 1935; 2 October is the conventional date of the Palazzo Venezia balcony declaration and was not independently verified in this pool. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from mussolini.journey.json.
stops.campa: From the balcony of the Palazzo Venezia, Benito Mussolini tells a filled square that Italy is at war with Ethiopia. Mussolini's own written authorization will put mustard gas, banned by treaty since 1925, into the bomb bays of aircraft flying over Ethiopian troops and villages. The Adwa defeat of 1896 is the debt he says he is collecting, thirty-nine years late. In Addis Ababa the emperor still has, in theory, an arbitration procedure running at Geneva, and it goes on running while the columns cross the Mareb.
suggested_refs: The balcony of the Palazzo Venezia, Rome
sources: mussolini.journey.json, 'Rome, Palazzo Venezia, war declared on Ethiopia'

stops.name: Addis Ababa, the general mobilization
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: The emperor issues the general mobilization order. Every man who can carry a rifle is called and those who cannot are told to bring spears; the old feudal levy assembles for the last time and marches north. Against it Italy brings aircraft, armor, and a chemical arsenal. Geneva has voted sanctions that exclude oil and leave the Suez Canal open to Italian troopships. He will command in person, because the custom of the Solomonic line requires the monarch to stand in the line when the country is invaded.
suggested_refs: The mobilization proclamation of 3 October 1935

stops.name: Dessie, the northern line breaks
stops.date_confidence: the Dessie headquarters and the February retreat are attested. The battle chronology is corrected here: First Tembien closed 24 January 1936, Amba Aradam ran 10-19 February 1936, Second Tembien closed 29 February, Shire ran 28 February into early March. An earlier working note placed these battles in October 1935, roughly four months early.
stops.campa: The emperor keeps his headquarters at Dessie while Badoglio's columns drive south through Tigray. The northern line built on Mekelle and Amba Aradam breaks in February: First Tembien closes in January, Amba Aradam falls between the tenth and the nineteenth of February, Second Tembien and Shire follow inside three weeks. What breaks the armies moving with him is not only artillery. Italian aircraft spray mustard gas across troops, herds and water in violation of the Geneva Protocol, and the levies come apart under it.
stops.quote: Special sprayers were installed on board aircraft so that they could vaporize, over vast areas of territory, a fine, death-dealing rain.
stops.quote_source: Appeal to the League of Nations, Geneva, 1936; Wikisource text. Spoken months later, describing what is happening here.
suggested_refs: The Italian chemical campaign of early 1936 and the Geneva Protocol of 1925
sources: Wikisource, 'Appeal to The League of Nations'

stops.name: Maychew, the emperor in the line
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Troop figures are the ranges given by Wikipedia's Second Italo-Ethiopian War article and are estimates. He had reached Korem on 3 March and decided there to give pitched battle rather than disperse into guerrilla resistance.
stops.campa: At Maychew the emperor commands in person, some thirty to thirty-five thousand men against roughly forty thousand Italian and colonial troops, having chosen open battle because the tradition of the throne requires the monarch to lead the decisive stand. Air power and gas break the formations, and the retreat descends into disarray. There is no conventional army left after this day and no conventional war left to fight. What remains is a choice between the mountains and the rostrum at Geneva, and he takes the rostrum.
stops.quote: soldiers, women, children, cattle, rivers, lakes and pastures were drenched continually with this deadly rain.
stops.quote_source: Appeal to the League of Nations, Geneva, 1936; Wikisource text
suggested_refs: The Maychew battlefield, 31 March 1936

stops.name: Lalibela, Bete Giyorgis in the retreat
stops.date_confidence: the war chronology places him at Lalibela on this date. What he did there is not recorded in any source reachable this session and is left as a gap rather than filled.
stops.campa: The retreating column enters Lalibela, where eleven churches are cut downward into volcanic rock, Bete Giyorgis among them, carved as a cross sunk in a pit. The chronology places him here on the thirteenth of April. What he does in the city is not recorded: whether he prays, rests, or holds a council of war, the sources do not say. The fleeing monarch of the Solomonic line spends a day inside the most sacred architecture his church possesses, and the record keeps no word of what he did in it.
suggested_refs: Bete Giyorgis and the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela

stops.name: Addis Ababa, the departure for exile
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He addresses the parliament, says the fight is not over, and leaves the capital for French Somaliland with his family. Behind him the city comes apart into looting before the Italians arrive to occupy it. Ahead is the railway to Djibouti that French engineers built and a British cruiser waiting at the end of it. He will not see Addis Ababa for five years. Emperors of Ethiopia have not, before this, left the country while a war was being fought inside it, and the departure is argued over in Addis Ababa for decades afterward.
suggested_refs: The last session of the Ethiopian parliament before the occupation, 2 May 1936

stops.name: Rome, Palazzo Venezia: the empire proclaimed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the mussolini journey file; Badoglio had entered Addis Ababa on 5 May. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from mussolini.journey.json.
stops.campa: Mussolini returns to the same balcony and proclaims Victor Emmanuel III Emperor of Ethiopia and himself First Marshal of the Empire. Badoglio's troops hold Addis Ababa; Italian East Africa is declared, joining Eritrea, Somaliland and Ethiopia under one crown. The League that seated Ethiopia in 1923 does not unseat Italy for taking it, and most of its members recognize the conquest within two years. A throne traced to Solomon is annexed by announcement from a square in Rome, to a man who has never been to Ethiopia.
suggested_refs: The proclamation of Italian East Africa, 9 May 1936
sources: mussolini.journey.json, 'Rome, Palazzo Venezia, the empire proclaimed'

stops.name: Djibouti, the cruiser at the quay
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: The imperial family boards the British cruiser HMS Enterprise at Djibouti. French Somaliland grants transit and nothing further, unwilling to provoke Rome. The port is Ethiopia's outlet to the sea, reached by the railway the French built, and it is now the threshold of exile. The ship sails north for Palestine rather than straight for England, a routing set by where the Mediterranean squadron happens to be rather than by anybody's plan for him. Nobody in London has decided yet what he is to be called.
suggested_refs: HMS Enterprise and the evacuation of the Ethiopian imperial family, May 1936

stops.name: Jerusalem, the compound revisited
stops.date_confidence: May 1936 is attested for the Haifa landfall and the passage to Jerusalem; the day is not fixed in any source reachable this session, and must postdate the sailing from Djibouti on 4 May. The 15th is a placeholder within the attested month, chosen only to preserve travel order.
stops.campa: The cruiser lands the party at Haifa, under British Mandate, and from there they go up to Jerusalem, where the Ethiopian imperial house keeps a residence beside the monastic community that has held its foothold in the city for centuries. He was here twelve years ago as a regent touring the capitals of the world. He is here now as a monarch without a country, waiting on a British decision about where he may be permitted to live. The holy sites are unchanged; the standing of the man praying at them is not.
suggested_refs: The Ethiopian compound in Jerusalem, refuge of the imperial family in May 1936

stops.name: Geneva, the appeal to the League
stops.date_confidence: contradiction flagged, not silently resolved. Wikipedia's Timeline of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War states '30 June 1936: Emperor Haile Selassie addresses the League of Nations', and that date is used here. The Wikisource text of the address is headed 7 June 1936. A third reading, 12 May 1936, comes from a misparse of the Haile Selassie article's sentence about the League granting him leave to address the assembly, and is physically impossible: he sailed from Djibouti only on 4 May. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from the interlock lens; the geography lens gives 46.2016, 6.1466 for the same Assembly hall.
stops.campa: He walks to the rostrum of the Assembly and speaks in Amharic. Italian journalists in the gallery jeer and are removed by the ushers. He describes the sprayers fitted to the aircraft, the gas falling on soldiers and herds and rivers, and the arbitration that ran on while the invasion was being prepared. Four years earlier this same body had commissioned Albert Einstein to write to Sigmund Freud asking whether war could be escaped. The Assembly hears the emperor out and votes to lift sanctions within weeks.
stops.quote: Representatives of the World, I have come to Geneva to discharge in your midst the most painful of the duties of the head of a State. What reply shall I have to take back to my people?
stops.quote_source: Appeal to the League of Nations, closing lines; English translation issued by the Haile Selassie I Press, text as hosted on Wikisource
suggested_refs: The Wikisource text of the Appeal to the League of Nations
The League's vote to lift sanctions against Italy, July 1936
sources: Wikisource, 'Appeal to The League of Nations'
Wikipedia, 'Timeline of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War'
einstein.journey.json, Caputh and the League of Nations

stops.name: Bath, Fairfield House
stops.date_confidence: the year of purchase and the residence through 1941 are attested; the month is not fixed in reachable sources, and July is chosen only to keep the house after the Geneva address in travel order. Coordinates corrected to Wikipedia's figure for Fairfield House on Kelston Road; two earlier working figures, 51.386, -2.3717 and 51.394, -2.383, both sat over a kilometre east. The 'fourteen-room' figure sometimes attached to the house is unsupported.
stops.campa: He buys Fairfield House on Kelston Road, on the north-west edge of Bath, and settles his household there for the duration. Before Bath the family stays at Warne's Hotel in Worthing and at a house called Parkside in Wimbledon. From this address he writes, receives petitioners and waits, while Ethiopia is administered as a province of Italian East Africa and the patriot bands in the highlands keep a war going that no government recognizes. In 1958 he gives the house to the city of Bath, which gives him its freedom.
suggested_refs: Fairfield House, Kelston Road, Bath, donated to the city in 1958

stops.name: Bath, the Christmas broadcast to America
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The deaths of Princess Romanework as an Italian prisoner and of Princess Tsehai in childbirth are attested to the exile period; Romanework's death is given as 1941 in the summary chronology, with some sources placing it differently.
stops.campa: With a fractured knee from a traffic accident he broadcasts a Christmas message to the United States from England. He is a head of state whose state has been abolished by the recognition of other states, speaking over the radio to a country that has not recognized the conquest and does not intend to do anything about it either. He asks the free nations to remember the weak ones looking toward their flags. Two of his daughters die in these years: Romanework in Italian captivity, Tsehai in childbirth in 1942.
stops.quote: People of America! I wish you a merry Christmas. I plead with you to remember in your prayers all those weak and endangered peoples who look to the flags of the free nations with confidence...
stops.quote_source: Christmas Broadcast to America, radio address of 25 December 1937; Wikisource text
suggested_refs: The Christmas Broadcast to America, 25 December 1937

stops.name: Khartoum, the forward base
stops.date_confidence: the source gives a range, 1940-1941, without month; month and day default to 01. Italy entered the war in June 1940, so the move to Khartoum cannot precede that.
stops.campa: Italy enters the world war and Britain, which had preferred not to notice him, discovers a use for the Emperor of Ethiopia. He is brought to Khartoum. From Sudanese territory the British organize irregular units, Ethiopian patriot columns and regular Commonwealth troops for the invasion of Italian East Africa. Exile turns back into campaign. The man who spent four years being a symbol in a Somerset garden becomes again the flag the highland bands are asked to rally to, and this time somebody is arming them.
suggested_refs: The East African Campaign staged from Sudan, 1940-1941

stops.name: Um Iddla, the border crossed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; coordinates approximate, Um Iddla is a minor crossing not consistently mapped across sources.
stops.campa: He crosses the border near Um Iddla and stands on Ethiopian ground for the first time in nearly five years. The imperial standard is raised. Addis Ababa is months and several hundred miles away, garrisoned still, and the fighting from here is done by patriot columns, Sudanese and Ethiopian regulars, and a small British irregular force. He walks back into his country at a crossing so minor that the maps do not agree on where it is. He had left it from the deck of a departing cruiser.
suggested_refs: The raising of the imperial standard at Um Iddla, 18 January 1941

stops.name: Addis Ababa, the return to the day
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the five-year symmetry with Badoglio's entry on 5 May 1936 is exact and was arranged.
stops.campa: He enters Addis Ababa on the fifth of May, five years to the day from the morning Badoglio's troops entered it, and the timing is deliberate, arranged by men who understood that a calendar can be made to answer back. Crowds line the route. The city has been through occupation, the Graziani reprisals, and the flight and return of most of its people. He addresses the Ethiopian nation and does not concede that the throne was ever vacant. The British, who hold the country militarily, spend the next three years being told it is not theirs to hold.
suggested_refs: The address to the Ethiopian people on the return to Addis Ababa, 5 May 1941

stops.name: Addis Ababa, slavery abolished under penalty of death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He signs the proclamation confirming the abolition of slavery throughout the empire, with penalties for slave trading that run as far as death. Ethiopia's League application in 1923 had been argued partly on this promise; Italy's case for invasion had been argued partly on its incompletion. The legal institution ends by decree from the palace that has been legislating it out of existence in stages since Menelik. What ends by decree and what ends in the districts are not the same date, and nobody in the palace pretends otherwise.
suggested_refs: The anti-slavery proclamation of 27 August 1942

stops.name: Shashamane, five hundred acres for the diaspora
stops.date_confidence: the 1948 designation is attested without a month, so month and day default to 01; the formal conveyance to the Ethiopian World Federation is dated to a 1955 letter, and settlers arrive from 1955 onward.
stops.campa: He sets aside five hundred acres at Shashamane for Black people of the diaspora who supported Ethiopia during the occupation; the land is conveyed formally to the Ethiopian World Federation in a letter of 1955, and settlers begin arriving. It becomes the physical address of repatriation for a movement that worships him and that he has never endorsed. After 1975 the successor government confiscates most of the grant under its policy against private land, and the settler population falls from more than two thousand to fewer than three hundred by 2004.
suggested_refs: The Shashamane land grant and the Twelve Tribes of Israel headquarters there

stops.name: Addis Ababa, Africa Hall: the charter signed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Signatory count hedged: Wikipedia gives 32 states in one place and 33 signatory governments in another, and the discrepancy is not resolved here. Coordinates corrected to Wikipedia's figure for Africa Hall; an earlier working figure of 9.0197, 38.7614 sat about 550 m off.
stops.campa: Thirty-two African heads of state sign the charter of the Organisation of African Unity at Africa Hall, and Haile Selassie takes the chair. He has spent the year brokering between the Casablanca bloc around Kwame Nkrumah and the Monrovia bloc around Leopold Sedar Senghor, and the charter is the document both will sign. Ethiopia's claim to host rests on never having been colonized, which requires the five Italian years to count as occupation rather than conquest. In 2009 Muammar Gaddafi takes the chair of its successor in this same city.
suggested_refs: Africa Hall, Addis Ababa, and the OAU Charter of 25 May 1963
sources: muammar_gaddafi.journey.json, 'Addis Ababa, the African Union chair'

stops.name: New York, the United Nations
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Coordinates are the UN headquarters figure from the geography lens; the quotes lens carries a coarser New York pin at 40.7128, -74.006 for the same address.
stops.campa: He addresses the General Assembly of the body that replaced the one he appealed to in 1936, and he opens by saying so. Twenty-seven years earlier he had mounted a rostrum in Geneva and been heard politely and left to it. The passage he delivers about race and inferiority is set to music by Bob Marley in 1976 as War, sung nearly verbatim, and reaches a larger audience through a reggae record than it ever reached through the United Nations. He speaks as a founding member of an organization his own dispossession helped argue into existence.
stops.quote: that until the philosophy which holds one race superior and another inferior is finally and permanently discredited and abandoned; that until there are no longer first class and second class citizens of any nation; that until the color of a man's skin is of no more significance than the color of his eyes; that until the basic human rights are equally guaranteed to all without regard to race; that until that day, the dream of lasting peace and world citizenship and the rule of international morality will remain but a fleeting illusion, to be pursued but never attained.
stops.quote_source: Address to the United Nations General Assembly, New York, 4 October 1963; Wikisource text
suggested_refs: The Wikisource text of the 1963 UN address
Bob Marley and the Wailers, 'War' (1976)

stops.name: Kingston, Palisadoes: Grounation Day
stops.date_confidence: the 21 April date and the commemorative practice are confirmed by Wikipedia's Rastafari article; the year 1966 is the one universally reported in secondary sources but was not explicit in the passage fetched, and is carried as reconstruction for the year alone. The instruction to seek liberation before repatriation is transmitted through Rastafari oral tradition.
stops.campa: The aircraft lands at Palisadoes at half past one and an estimated hundred thousand Rastafari are on the tarmac and the fences, waiting for a god. He does not walk the red carpet; he makes contact with the ground, and the date becomes Grounation Day. He meets elders including Mortimer Planno, gives out gold medallions bearing the Ethiopian seal, and by tradition tells them to liberate Jamaica before repatriating to Africa. Simon Bolivar wrote the Jamaica Letter in this city in 1815, and Christopher Columbus was marooned a year up the coast at St Ann's Bay.
suggested_refs: Palisadoes Airport, Kingston, 21 April 1966
The annual observance of Grounation Day
sources: columbus.journey.json, 'St Ann's Bay, Jamaica: the year marooned'

stops.name: Addis Ababa, deposed by the Derg
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the deposition and the end of the monarchy. The causes named here, the concealed famine, the army pay revolts and the student movement, are general context rather than claims sourced in this pool, and are carried as reconstruction.
stops.campa: The Derg, a committee of junior officers, deposes him and abolishes the monarchy. A famine his government had concealed, revolts over army pay, and the students have taken the throne apart across eight months of creeping proclamations. He is removed from the palace under guard. The Solomonic line ends. Within three years Fidel Castro will be sending Cuban troops into the Ogaden to fight for the government that replaced him, in the same desert where the Welwel wells gave Mussolini his war.
suggested_refs: The Derg proclamation deposing Haile Selassie, 12 September 1974

stops.name: Addis Ababa, Jubilee Palace: the death in custody
stops.date_confidence: date attested. Cause contested and left contested: the Derg's 1975 statement gave circulatory failure following prostate surgery, while later testimony in the Red Terror proceedings alleged strangulation or smothering on Mengistu Haile Mariam's order. Coordinates for the Jubilee Palace differ between lenses, 9.0227/38.7615 and 9.025/38.7469; the Wikipedia article on the palace returns 404, so neither could be verified and the first is used as approximate.
stops.campa: He dies in custody at the Jubilee Palace, eighty-three years old, eleven months after the deposition. The Derg announces circulatory failure following prostate surgery. Testimony given later, in the proceedings against former Derg officials, says he was smothered on Mengistu Haile Mariam's order. The two accounts have never been reconciled and are not reconciled here. The body is buried in secret on the palace grounds, reportedly under a slab beneath a latrine, and lies there while the men who put it there hold the country.
suggested_refs: The Red Terror trials of former Derg officials, 1992-94
sources: Amnesty International and Ethiopian court testimony as cited in secondary histories

stops.name: Addis Ababa, Holy Trinity Cathedral: the reburial
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the exhumation is dated to 1992, during the Red Terror investigations. Coordinates corrected to Wikipedia's figure for Holy Trinity Cathedral; two earlier working figures, 9.018/38.758 and 9.0184/38.7598, both sat about 1.6 km off.
stops.campa: Twenty-five years after the death the remains, exhumed from the palace grounds in 1992, are given a funeral at Holy Trinity Cathedral and interred in the north transept beside Empress Menen. The Ethiopian state does not declare it a state funeral. Rastafari pilgrims come from Jamaica and Britain and elsewhere, and some Rastafari organizations refuse to attend at all, on the grounds that a man who did not die cannot be buried. The cathedral holds what it holds, and the argument about what that is continues outside it.
suggested_refs: The north transept of Holy Trinity Cathedral, Addis Ababa

stops.name: Cannizaro Park, Wimbledon: the bust thrown down
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The bust by Hilda Seligman is dated 1957 in the source.
stops.campa: The bronze bust that Hilda Seligman made of him, standing in Cannizaro Park since 1957 near the house where he stayed during the exile, has been a pilgrimage stop for London Rastafari for sixty years. On the thirtieth of June 2020 a crowd of about a hundred, reported as connected to unrest in Ethiopia after the killing of the singer Hachalu Hundessa the day before, pulls it down and breaks it. The quarrel is Oromo and it is current. The statue was standing in a public garden in south London, four thousand miles from it.
suggested_refs: Hilda Seligman's bust of Haile Selassie, Cannizaro Park, 1957-2020
